source.title: Automatically Finding and Validating Unexpected Side-Effects of Interventions on Language Models
source.authors: Quintin Pope; A. Balaji; Jacques Thibodeau; Xiaoli Z. Fern

record.tranche_reason: The study applies a Harry Potter unlearning variant as an intervention in a behavioral audit, but does not test whether attacks recover the targeted knowledge.
record.gate_note: The study compares generations from a base model and an unlearning variant across prompt banks, reporting near-null results on Persona and TruthfulQA and modest completion-related differences on BOLD. These are findings about off-target behavioral effects, not recovery after fine-tuning, activation edits, quantization, or prompting; none of the claim versions is tested.
record.test_reason: The study uses the Harry Potter unlearned Llama-2-7B as one case study for its behavioural-auditing pipeline. It reports only off-target generation differences: near-null on Persona and TruthfulQA, and modest completion degradation on BOLD. It never measures Harry Potter knowledge, general-capability benchmarks, or any recovery attack (fine-tuning, ablation, quantization, prompting), so none of versions A–F is tested. The BOLD degradation is a related construct (off-target side effects on completion quality, judged by an LLM discriminator's AUC), not the near-chance-forgetting-plus-preserved-ability claim of A.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct. The authors find Harry Potter unlearning yields almost no detectable differences on Persona and TruthfulQA. It shows modest spillover on BOLD entity completions (reduced completeness, factuality and informativeness), which they describe as mild (max AUC 0.644).
record.recipe_differences: The paper evaluates an existing Harry Potter unlearning variant as a case study; it does not reproduce or compare recovery recipes.
record.method_sensitivity: The observed side effects depend on prompt bank: BOLD surfaces completion degradation that is not statistically discoverable with Persona or TruthfulQA prompts.

fits_no_version.finding: The Harry Potter unlearning variant shows near-null differences from base on Persona and TruthfulQA (mean AUC 0.50 and 0.47, close to zero validated hypotheses). On entity-centric BOLD completions it shows modest, validated degradation: blanks, generic filler, more factual errors; about 10 validated hypotheses, within-context AUC 0.588, max 0.644. The near-null Unlearning result holds across three discriminator models (Table 11).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Approximate (Harry Potter) unlearning has mild, domain-conditional off-target effects on factual completion quality while leaving persona-style behaviour essentially unchanged.

record.problems: The results depend on the selected prompt banks, and the paper notes that rare or adversarial behaviors may be missed. The unlearning result is based on one model variant and the reported BOLD effect is described as mild; no direct targeted-knowledge recovery attack or general-capability evaluation is performed.

untested.parts: Targeted (Harry Potter) knowledge accuracy, general-ability benchmarks and resistance to attacks are not measured. Off-target completion degradation is recorded under fits_no_version, not as a test of A.
No activation ablation and no blocking-vs-deletion analysis.
Both models were loaded in 8-bit only for decoding. No quantization recovery test, and Harry Potter knowledge is never probed.
No rephrasing, jailbreak, multilingual or in-context recovery attempts.
No robust unlearning method is proposed or tested.

record.verdict_notes: Eldan & Russinovich (Who's Harry Potter?) is an original source, but this study is not; it only uses the released unlearned model. Both models were quantized to 8-bit via BitsAndBytes for decoding. This is not a recovery experiment, and no Harry Potter prompts were used, so it says nothing about version D. The rows' states describe the pipeline's discriminability measure, not any claim version, so versions stay ["none"]. R3 'partial' reflects the authors' 'modest' framing. The study is primarily an auditing/detection-method paper.

versions.untested_parts: Does not measure targeted-knowledge accuracy, preservation of general ability, or whether attacks recover knowledge.
No relearning or fine-tuning attack is applied.
No activation direction is ablated and no analysis tests whether knowledge is blocked from access rather than deleted.
No quantization attack is tested as a recovery method.
No prompt rephrasing, jailbreak, other-language prompt, or in-context recovery test is conducted.
No method is tested for resisting the recovery attacks listed in the claim.

tranche.reason: Harry Potter unlearning is a case study for the paper's side-effect auditing pipeline. It reports off-target behaviour differences, not recovery of unlearned knowledge.

source_check.notes: All three rows match the text. The Table 3 caption states three runs. The BOLD spillover (an LLM-judged discriminability AUC, not a capability score) is context for version A's 'keeping general ability' but does not measure target knowledge or recovery, so versions none is right.
